messages:
Maya L: Quick update — rolled out async write-behind + eviction hinting to the Redis KV prefix cache in canary and seeing a 22-30% drop in p95 tail latency for chat workloads (32k seq). Per-token GPU cost down ~18% in the canary traffic slice. :tada:

Zack H: awesome. quick question — is this the async write-behind we prototyped last sprint or a new approach?

Maya L: same idea but implemented as an opt-in Redis Lua script + local write queue on the runtime. Key differences: non-blocking cache population on miss (response returns while population async), and lightweight LRU hint commands we push to the cluster to reduce eviction thrash for hot prefixes.

Julia R: can you paste the rollout plan and the flag names? want to make sure monitoring + SLOs are wired before broad rollout.

Maya L: rollout summary:
1) Canary (5% traffic) for 24h — done, no regressions.
2) Increment to 25% over 4h windows if p95 and error-rate stable.
3) 100% after 48h of validation.

Flags: `runtime.cache.async_writebehind` = true/false
Per-tenant opt-out: `runtime.cache.prefetch_mode = none|sync|async`

Command to flip in prod (ops runbook):
```bash
# update feature flag in config service
curl -X POST $CONFIG_SVC/flags -d '{"key":"runtime.cache.async_writebehind","value":true}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
# trigger rolling restart of runtime pods in canary pool
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-canary -n prod
```

infra-bot: Canary deployment finished: runtime-canary v2025.11.3 -> success. Observed: 22% p95 latency drop, 17% median cost decrease. No increase in 5xx.

Kevin S: memory question — pushing more hot prefixes into Redis could increase memory usage. did we see pressure on the cluster?

Maya L: saw a modest +9% memory use in canary. Mitigations:
- eviction hinting reduces churn so net working set is smaller over time
- we set per-tenant prefix caps (defaults tuned to production tail)
- fallback path kicks in when Redis memory > 85% (runtime bypasses cache and uses model directly)

Snippet of the Lua hint we use (sanitized):
```lua
-- hint.lua
redis.call('HINCRBY', 'prefix-hint', KEYS[1], 1)
if tonumber(redis.call('TTL', KEYS[1])) < 0 then
  redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])
end
return 1
```

Julia R: monitoring hooks? where are the dashboards / traces for verifying cognitive quality + perf combined?

Maya L: dashboards added to Console -> Runtime -> CacheHotPaths. Metrics: `cache.hit_rate`, `cache.local_queue_latency_ms`, `cache.async_pop_latency_ms`, and `model.cost_per_token`. Traces: sample traces tagged `cache_async=true`. Link: https://console.internal/redwood/runtime/cache/canary (internal)

Zack H: regressions / evals? did this change affect generation quality?

Maya L: ran the nightly eval suite + 3 customer-specific prompt sets — no measurable quality regressions. We also inserted a gating test in the CI that compares token-level logprobs on a small prompt set before allowing the flag to be promoted.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook added: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/async-kvcache (includes rollback, diagnostics, and how to force per-tenant opt-out).

Kevin S: any ops commands to force disable for a tenant if they report issues?

Maya L: yep — per-tenant override: `curl -X POST $CONFIG_SVC/tenant/{id}/overrides -d '{"runtime.cache.prefetch_mode":"none"}'` — immediate take effect, no rollout needed.

Zack H: do we need a config to limit write-behind queue size per runtime? that was a problem on the prototype.

Maya L: good call — `runtime.cache.write_queue_limit` default=1024, and we implemented backpressure: beyond limit, writes are dropped and we log a `cache.write_dropped` metric. Backpressure threshold alarms added to PagerDuty.

Julia R: i'll add the new metrics to the SLO dashboard and notify CS about the opt-out path in case customers ping.

Maya L: thanks all. plan is to move to 25% in 2h if the next 30m of p95 trends flat. will post updates. :rocket:
